input: Research tuition costs for private music conservatories

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing who this research is for (e.g., the user themselves, a child, a student they advise) shapes which programs, degree levels, and costs are relevant.
The geographic scope (U.S. only, specific region, international) dramatically changes which conservatories are included and how costs are compared.
The specific instrument or music discipline (classical piano, jazz, voice, composition, etc.) determines which conservatories are even worth researching.
The degree or program level (undergraduate, graduate, diploma, summer program) determines the type of tuition figures to look for.
A budget ceiling or target tuition range would filter out institutions immediately and focus the research on affordable or accessible options.
Knowing what output is needed (a side-by-side comparison, a ranked list, a single recommendation) defines how thorough and structured the research must be.
Understanding when this information is needed (e.g., an application deadline approaching) sets urgency and determines how deep the research should go.

gold.taskTitle: Research tuition costs for private music conservatories
gold.taskDescription: Gather and compare tuition cost information for private music conservatories to support a decision or inquiry.

questions.title: Who is this tuition research being done for?
questions.description: Identify whether the research is for the user personally, a child, a student they mentor, or someone else — this shapes which programs and level of detail matter.

questions.title: Which countries or regions should be included?
questions.description: Determine the geographic scope — U.S. only, North America, Europe, or worldwide — to define which conservatories are in scope.

questions.title: What instrument or music discipline is the focus?
questions.description: Clarify whether this is for classical performance, jazz, voice, composition, conducting, or another discipline, as conservatory strengths and costs vary by specialty.

questions.title: What degree or program level is being considered?
questions.description: Establish whether the target is an undergraduate degree, graduate degree, artist diploma, or a shorter program like a summer intensive.

questions.title: Is there a maximum annual tuition budget in mind?
questions.description: Identify any hard budget ceiling so that unaffordable institutions can be excluded and the research stays relevant.

questions.title: What should the final output of this research look like?
questions.description: Determine the desired deliverable — a comparison table, a ranked shortlist, a single best recommendation, or raw notes — to calibrate how structured and detailed the work needs to be.

questions.title: When does this information need to be ready?
questions.description: Understand the urgency — an imminent application deadline vs. general long-term planning — to set the appropriate depth and pace of research.
